### Completed
- Added a responsive game interface and styling in `index.html` and `style.css`.
- Added Luma tokenization, parsing, bytecode compilation, VM/runtime, grid rendering, game controls, and three campaign levels in `game.js`.

### Active
- Validate the game in a browser and fix any implementation bugs.
- Confirm the default level is playable and the campaign can be completed.

### Blocked
- (none)

2. Run the game locally and capture/inspect a small JPEG screenshot.
3. Finish with a concise summary and note assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface, editor, level stats, world view, dialogs, language reference.
- `style.css`: Responsive dark-themed game styling and board visuals.
- `game.js`: Language engine, VM, gameplay logic, levels, and UI interactions.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- The user’s request remains to deliver the playable game; no completion note or validation has been provided yet.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable browser game that invents a complex programming-language engine.

## Requirements
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- The game is BYTEBOUND, a programming puzzle campaign using the fictional language Luma.
- The campaign has three sectors, a code editor, compiler/runtime, grid puzzles, and collectible memory shards.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created the responsive game interface and styling in `index.html` and `style.css`.
- Began implementing the Luma tokenizer, parser, compiler, VM, world rendering, and campaign levels in `game.js`.

### Active
- Repair and complete `game.js`; the latest rewrite is incomplete and needs syntax and runtime validation.
- Test gameplay, including level progression, then capture and inspect a current small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- `node --check game.js` previously failed with `SyntaxError: Unexpected token '}'`; `game.js` has since been replaced with a partial rewrite and has not been rechecked.

## Next Move
1. Continue implementing the game UI and runtime logic in `game.js`, then run `node --check game.js`.
2. Run the game in a browser and test the parser, actions, puzzle completion, and campaign progression.
3. Save and inspect a small JPEG screenshot, then finish with a concise summary and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface, editor, stats, world view, dialogs, and language reference.
- `style.css`: Responsive dark-themed game styling and board visuals.
- `game.js`: Language engine, VM/runtime, gameplay logic, levels, and UI interactions; currently incomplete.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Existing interface buttons and controls expect corresponding DOM elements and event handlers in `game.js`.
